headline: Ex-MP Akhtaruzzaman arrested over airport assault and disorder
summary: The former lawmaker and Jamaat-e-Islami leader was detained by DB police from his home in Dhaka Cantonment following a dispute at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.
details: Former lawmaker Major (retd) Akhtaruzzaman, who joined Jamaat-e-Islami last year, was arrested by a team of detectives from his home in Dhaka Cantonment around 6:00pm today.
The arrest follows a case filed over allegations that he assaulted a security official and created disorder at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport (HSIA) yesterday.
The incident occurred near the baggage belt area after passengers arriving from Madinah on Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight BG-338 faced delays in receiving luggage and a shortage of trolleys.
According to the complaint, Akhtaruzzaman became agitated and verbally abused the airport's Executive Director, Group Captain SM Ragib Samad, threatening to beat him and throw him out.
The situation escalated when Akhtaruzzaman allegedly assaulted security supervisor Warrant Officer Mohammad Kamal Uddin after being asked not to film in a restricted Key Point Installation area.
It is further alleged that he threw bottles of Zamzam water off trolleys, damaging them, and behaved aggressively toward a Biman Bangladesh Airlines representative.
The complainant stated that these actions obstructed officials from performing their duties at a sensitive installation and risked disrupting security at the airport.
Police are using CCTV footage, security records, and witness accounts as part of the ongoing investigation.
caption:
A former lawmaker and Jamaat-e-Islami leader has been arrested for allegedly assaulting security staff at Dhaka airport.

Former lawmaker Major (retd) Akhtaruzzaman, who joined Jamaat-e-Islami last year, was arrested by a team of detectives from his home in Dhaka Cantonment around 6:00pm today.

The arrest follows a case filed over allegations that he assaulted a security official and created disorder at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport (HSIA) yesterday.

The incident occurred near the baggage belt area after passengers arriving from Madinah on Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight BG-338 faced delays in receiving luggage and a shortage of trolleys.

According to the complaint, Akhtaruzzaman became agitated and verbally abused the airport's Executive Director, Group Captain SM Ragib Samad, threatening to beat him and throw him out.

The situation escalated when Akhtaruzzaman allegedly assaulted security supervisor Warrant Officer Mohammad Kamal Uddin after being asked not to film in a restricted Key Point Installation area.

It is further alleged that he threw bottles of Zamzam water off trolleys, damaging them, and behaved aggressively toward a Biman Bangladesh Airlines representative.

The complainant stated that these actions obstructed officials from performing their duties at a sensitive installation and risked disrupting security at the airport.

Police are using CCTV footage, security records, and witness accounts as part of the ongoing investigation.

topic: seven killed in Mymensingh road accident
headline_marked: 7 killed in Mymensingh crash, [[4 members of one family dead]]
headline: 7 killed in Mymensingh crash, 4 members of one family dead
summary: A child, mother, grandfather, and great-grandmother were among those killed when a bus and a CNG-run auto-rickshaw collided head-on in Mymensingh.
details: At least seven people were killed in a head-on collision between a Rajib Paribahan bus and a CNG-run auto-rickshaw in the Gandrapa area of Akua Bypass Road in Mymensingh today.
The victims, including three women, a child, and the CNG driver, all died at the scene. The auto-rickshaw was completely mangled in the crash.
Four members of the same family from Jamalpur Sadar upazila were among the deceased: Mofazzal Hossain Lebu (50), his mother Rashida Begum (70), his daughter Morjina (25), and his grandson Minal (5).
The family members were traveling to Gazipur when the accident occurred. Police are still working to identify the remaining three victims.
Police initially suspect that excessive speed by both vehicles caused the collision. Both the bus and the auto-rickshaw have been seized for investigation.
The tragedy sparked anger among local residents, who demanded stricter measures to prevent reckless driving on the highway.
